nyciml-2006-07-spring-sophfrosh-02.title: Drop altitudes
nyciml-2006-07-spring-sophfrosh-02.body:
The bases are $7$ and $13$ and the legs are $5$. Dropping altitudes from the ends of the short base cuts off $\frac{13 - 7}{2} = 3$ on each side, so the height is $\sqrt{25 - 9} = 4$. A diagonal spans horizontally $13 - 3 = 10$ and vertically $4$, so its length is $\sqrt{100 + 16} = \sqrt{116} = 2\sqrt{29}$.

**Answer: $2\sqrt{29}$**

nyciml-2006-07-spring-sophfrosh-02.title: Ptolemy's theorem
nyciml-2006-07-spring-sophfrosh-02.body:
An isosceles trapezoid is cyclic, so Ptolemy gives $d^2 = 7\cdot13 + 5\cdot5 = 116$, and $d = 2\sqrt{29}$.

**Answer: $2\sqrt{29}$**

nyciml-2006-07-spring-sophfrosh-03.title: Use a convenient distance
nyciml-2006-07-spring-sophfrosh-03.body:
Say the route is $60$ miles. Going takes $2$ hours. For an average of $40$ mph over $120$ miles, the whole trip takes $3$ hours, so the return takes $1$ hour: $60$ mph.

**Answer: 60 mph**

nyciml-2006-07-spring-sophfrosh-03.title: Harmonic mean
nyciml-2006-07-spring-sophfrosh-03.body:
For equal distances the average speed is the harmonic mean: $\frac{2}{\frac1{30} + \frac1v} = 40$, so $\frac1{30} + \frac1v = \frac1{20}$ and $\frac1v = \frac1{60}$, $v = 60$.

**Answer: 60 mph**

nyciml-2006-07-spring-sophfrosh-13.title: Cycle of 7
nyciml-2006-07-spring-sophfrosh-13.body:
The units digit of $2007^n$ is that of $7^n$, which cycles $7, 9, 3, 1$ with period $4$. Since $2007 = 4\cdot501 + 3$, the units digit is the third in the cycle: $3$.

**Answer: 3**

nyciml-2006-07-spring-sophfrosh-16.title: Complete the exponents
nyciml-2006-07-spring-sophfrosh-16.body:
$252 = 2^2\cdot3^2\cdot7$. To make every exponent a multiple of $3$, multiply by $2\cdot3\cdot7^2 = 294$. Then $252\cdot294 = 74088 = 42^3$.

**Answer: 294**

nyciml-2006-07-spring-sophfrosh-17.title: Odd plus even
nyciml-2006-07-spring-sophfrosh-17.body:
The sum is odd exactly when one ball is odd and one is even. There are $8$ odd and $7$ even numbers, so $8\cdot7 = 56$ such pairs out of $\binom{15}{2} = 105$: probability $\frac{56}{105} = \frac{8}{15}$.

**Answer: $\frac{8}{15}$**

nyciml-2006-07-spring-sophfrosh-17.title: Sequential draws
nyciml-2006-07-spring-sophfrosh-17.body:
Whatever the first ball, the second must have the other parity. $P = \frac{8}{15}\cdot\frac7{14} + \frac{7}{15}\cdot\frac{8}{14} = \frac{112}{210} = \frac8{15}$.

**Answer: $\frac{8}{15}$**

nyciml-2006-07-spring-sophfrosh-18.title: Divisible by 8 and 9
nyciml-2006-07-spring-sophfrosh-18.body:
For divisibility by $8$, the last three digits $\overline{7ab}$ must be a multiple of $8$: $700 = 8\cdot87 + 4$, so $\overline{ab} \equiv 4 \pmod 8$: $\overline{ab} \in \{04, 12, 20, 28, 36, 44, 52, 60, 68, 76, 84, 92\}$. For divisibility by $9$, the digit sum $3+0+2+5+8+6+7+a+b = 31 + a + b$ must be a multiple of $9$, so $a + b = 5$ or $14$. The only candidate is $68$ ($6 + 8 = 14$).

**Answer: $(a, b) = (6, 8)$**
